rachel: Heads-up — onboarding team flagged another confusing error example in the TypeScript quickstart. The sample shows checking status code numbers directly which led people to write brittle backoffs. Can we align on typed errors + a tiny retry_hint field in SDK errors?

omar: Totally. Current quickstart uses: ```if (err.status === 429) { backoff(1000) }``` which is fragile (headers/JSON envelope variation). Proposal: SDK surfaces classes (RateLimitError, AuthError, PermissionError, ServerError, ClientError) and each has `retryHint` : "no-retry" | "retry-after" | "exponential" | "refresh-token" plus `raw` (original payload/headers).

li: Would help. For TypeScript I'd expect `instanceof RateLimitError` and `err.retryAfter` (number | null). For Go, we can do interface methods `RetryHint() string` and `RetryAfter() time.Duration`. We need canonical parsing for `Retry-After` header (seconds / HTTP-date).

andrew: Quick nit: we sometimes get `429` with `Retry-After: 0` meaning try immediately (throttled but burst allowed). SDKs should treat numeric zero as "retry immediately" not as no-retry. Also some downstream infra returns `retry_hint` in JSON as "exponential". If present, SDK should prefer the explicit machine field over header heuristics.

rachel: Good point. How about this mapping doc snippet for onboarding: 
``
HTTP -> SDK
401 -> AuthError (retryHint: refresh-token if token-based)
403 -> PermissionError (no-retry)
429 -> RateLimitError (retryHint: retry-after if header present; else exponential)
5xx -> ServerError (retryHint: exponential)
4xx-other -> ClientError (no-retry)
``
Keep `httpStatus`, `rawBody`, and `headers` available on the exception.

omar: That looks clear. Can we add a tiny code example to the quickstart for TypeScript and Go showing the recommended pattern? E.g., TS: ```try { await client.generate(...) } catch (err) { if (err instanceof RateLimitError) { const t = err.retryAfter ?? backoffEstimate(); await sleep(t); } else throw err }``` and Go: ```if rl, ok := err.(interface{ RetryAfter() time.Duration }); ok { time.Sleep(rl.RetryAfter()) }```

li: I'll add helper funcs in go-sdk: `IsRetryable(err error) bool`, `RetryAfter(err error) time.Duration`, and `RetryHint(err error) string`. Tests should cover `Retry-After: 120`, `Retry-After: Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:02:00 GMT`, and missing header + `retry_hint: exponential` in json.

ci-bot: ci/go-sdk #789 failed: examples/quickstart_test.go:18 -> expected retry hint "retry-after" but got "none". https://ci.internal/redwood/go-sdk/789

andrew: Oof — looks like one of the mocked server responses didn't include headers in the test harness. li, can you patch tests to include header variants?

li: On it. Will also add a small end-to-end in sample-apps that spins up a tiny mock and demonstrates both header and body `retry_hint`.

rachel: After we merge, ops can update the onboarding quickstart to show `err.retryHint` usage and a recommended backoff snippet. This should reduce the number of "why did my client not retry" tickets.

omar: One more suggestion: add a linter rule in sample-app CI that flags direct numeric status checks like `err.status === 429` and suggests `instanceof RateLimitError` or `IsRetryable(err)`. That'll teach new users the right pattern.

andrew: +1. I'll put the linter rule in the sample-apps pre-commit.

li: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/go-sdk/pulls/472 -> implements typed errors + Retry-After parsing + helpers. Tests updated.

ci-bot: merge pipeline for PR 472 started.

rachel: Thanks everyone — big DX win for new users. Will follow up to make sure docs/examples are updated across ts/go/python before the next release. :rocket:
